# f09 redesign: maths check (11 November 2026)

**Disposition: changes required before plates or voice.** Exact rational calculations are in `work/brief240/f09-calculations.json`, generated by `check-f09.py`; the financial model carries full precision between periods. The $30,000 loan gives balances $29,580, $29,157.48 and $28,732.42488; month 59 balance is $372.57570429365, and the reduced final payment is $374.8111585194. The design's author verification says A59 is 372.5844..., which is wrong: correct it. The displayed closed-form working subtracts rounded $1,810.82 from rounded $30,543.25 to give $28,732.42; those displayed figures subtract to $28,732.43. Show additional precision or make clear the calculation uses unrounded terms. Likewise independently rounded final interest $2.24 and principal $372.58 sum to $374.82, one cent more than the displayed $374.81; explain the independent rounding or reconcile the displayed split.

The recurrence assumes interest before the end-of-period payment. A falling balance is not automatic: for positive r the balance is unchanged when M=rP and grows initially when M<rP; scope the slow-then-faster description to an amortising loan. The geometric closed form divides by r and requires r≠0; for zero interest A_n=P−nM. Annual-rate division by 12 assumes a nominal annual rate compounded monthly. The $400,000 example with exact r=1/240 and $2,147.29 payments has A180=$271,534.70 and crosses below $200,000 at A242=$199,834.68. A full 360th payment overpays by about $2.92; the last payment is about $2,144.37 under the stated full-precision convention, not a full $2,147.29. Label the payoff and rate as approximate and retain the smaller-final-payment qualification.

Live source checked 11 November: https://hscscience.com.au/subjects/maths-advanced/year12/financial-mathematics/lesson12.sa.html Problem 1 uses the same $30,000, 7.2%, $600 and first two balances but gives A3=$28,732.43 in error; Problem 2's total interest $532.42 is consistent with the corrected $28,732.42. https://hscscience.com.au/subjects/maths-advanced/year12/financial-mathematics/lesson13.sa.html card 04 states $2,147.29.
